implementation.name: original-v2-tinytl-architecture
implementation.scope: The original three-block comparison. Saved input tiles are schematic, not a memory-byte model. TinyTL freezes backbone weights and trains biases, lite residuals, and the classifier. Mask and normalization state may be retained or recomputed.
implementation.question: Why does a frozen backbone still need a backward pass?

purpose: Why does a frozen backbone still need a backward pass?
storyboard: Both models hold persistent weights. Full fine-tuning marks backbone weights trainable; TinyTL keeps them frozen. No saved input tile is live yet.
Full fine-tuning retains the shown full input for block 1. TinyTL retains the smaller lite-residual input shown for that block; its frozen backbone weights remain available.
Both models advance through block 2 and retain the state needed by its later backward consumers. Earlier saved inputs remain live.
The third block executes. Three block-input records are now live in each schematic, with different state requirements.
The classifier receives its input. Its saved input joins the block records; none can be released before its last backward consumer.
The classifier computes its gradients and passes an activation gradient to block 3. The shown classifier input can now be released.

The activation gradient traverses block 3 in both models. Full fine-tuning forms its weight gradients; TinyTL forms bias and lite-residual gradients without changing the frozen backbone weight. The consumed saved input is released.
Backward traverses the second frozen TinyTL block as well. Only after its consumers finish is its shown saved input released.
Backward reaches the first block in both models. Its saved input is consumed and released. Frozen weights did not truncate gradient propagation.

Full fine-tuning updates all trainable weights. TinyTL updates biases, lite residuals, and the classifier; the backbone weights keep their original values. These tiles are saved inputs, not total training memory.
guard: Frozen backbone weights never change, but backward traverses all three blocks. Only saved-input state is illustrated; masks, normalization, gradient storage, and total training memory are not quantified. Parameter updates occur only at optimizer step.
